author: Henry James
title: The Turn of the Screw, in The Two Magics
edition: New York: The Macmillan Company; London: Macmillan & Co., Ltd., 1898. Scan-backed Wikisource transcription of this edition; chapter headings, navigation and page-number anchors omitted from prose excerpts; HTML line-wrapping whitespace collapsed. The library text holds the whole volume's fiction: The Turn of the Screw (the untitled prologue and Chapters I to XXIV) and Covering End (Chapters I to VIII), each under its printed title and chapter numerals; the title page, contents and publisher's advertisements are omitted. The Wikisource Covering End Chapter 7 page also transcludes the opening of Chapter VIII from the shared scan page; that repeated passage is kept once, under Chapter VIII. The Turn of the Screw, Chapters XI to XXIV, was collated on 2026-11-18 word by word against the OCR of Internet Archive twomagicsturnofs00jameiala (the scan behind the Wikisource transcription) and against Project Gutenberg 42486, each difference decided on the page images: the transcription had modernised that text, and fifty-six readings were changed to the print in forty-one paragraphs: word forms (“none the less” four times for “nonetheless”, “fulness”, “afterwards”, “unmistakeably”, “for ever”), hyphened compounds (“half-a-dozen”, “fairy-tale”, “break-down”, “out-of-doors”, “church-bells”, “house-door”, “mooring-place”, “half-way”, “tea-things”, “dressing-table”, “dining-room”, “wedding-journey”, “off-hand”), words (“elate”, “now permit”, “or of a discussion”, and “about”, “a feeling”, “and that now”, “a reference” restored), punctuation in twenty-two places, three long dashes, and one straight quotation mark made curly like the rest. The prologue and Chapters I to X, which the school nights read, were not changed: a comparison with the same scan shows the same kind of modernisation there (for example “favor”, “color”, “learned” and “afterward” for the print’s “favour”, “colour”, “learnt” and “afterwards”), left for a pass that may re-hash those nights.

rights.basis: This 1898 English-language edition was published before 1931 and is in the US public domain as of 2026; only James’s narrative is supplied, with no modern annotation.

Only the transcluded scan text is used: Wikisource headers, page-number anchors and zero-width page-boundary characters removed (the transcription has no footnotes); the Covering End title page dropped; story titles and chapter numerals became headings; paragraphs joined with whitespace collapsed; emphasis flattened. On 2026-11-18 blocks 388 to 810 (The Turn of the Screw, Chapters XI to XXIV) were corrected in forty-one paragraphs after collating them against the page images of IA twomagicsturnofs00jameiala, as the edition note records; no block was added, removed or split.
